Q: Testing In App Purchases on TestFlight A:

2026 UPDATE

The original question is 10 years old but remains relevant. The answer by Vvk (also 10 years old) refers to iTunes Connect, which is out of date, and talks about sandbox accounts, which are indeed important, but may not be applicable when considering beta testers.

This answer covers various testing pathways (not just TestFlight that was in the question) and makes the important distinction between the 'sandbox environment' and 'sandbox accounts'.

The following is based on my recent experience (Jan 2026).

See also Apple documentation:

  • Testing at all stages of development with Xcode and the sandbox
  • Testing In-App Purchases with sandbox

Setting things up

  1. In App Store Connect, go to Apps, select your app, the Distribution tab and then In-App Purchases. Create your product(s) and/or subscription(s). Complete all the information required. The product image is optional but the Review Information screenshot is required. Without this, your status will be stuck at "Missing Metadata". Once you have provided all this and saved, your status should be "Ready to Submit".
  2. In your app, write the code to purchase those products/subscriptions.
  3. In preparation for the next public release, begin to prepare a new submission. In the section In-App Purchases and Subscriptions add your products/subscriptions.
  4. Within your Apple Developer Account, you need to set up payment and tax details and agree to an extra set of terms and conditions.
  5. Optionally, set up sandbox accounts. In App Store Connect, go to Users and Access, then Sandbox and add Test Accounts. These must be Apple IDs. If you use an email provider that supports + filtering, like Gmail, then you can use this (e.g. your_email_address+sandbox1@gmail.com), but you'll still need to create an Apple ID for it.

Testing via Xcode

From Xcode, there are 2 ways of testing in-app purchases:

Local testing via Xcode

  • Add a .storekit file to your project. You can set not just the product details (currency, price, etc.) but also testing scenarios, such as network connection failures, withdrawn product or 'Ask to Buy'.
  • Enable it (Product > Edit Scheme > Run (tab) > Options > StoreKit Configuration).
  • Run your app on a physical device from Xcode. When you try to make a purchase, you'll get the Apple payment dialog with title "Xcode" and the message "For testing purposes only. You will not be charged for confirming this purchase." Transactions can be seen and managed within Xcode.

Note that this is the only way you can test scenarios like 'Ask to Buy' or refunds.

Sandbox environment testing via Xcode

  • Set StoreKit Configuration to None and run the app from Xcode. Product details will now come from your App Store Account within the sandbox environment. The Apple payment dialog has the title "Sandbox" and same "For testing purposes only..." message, but note that it still shows your Apple account at the bottom of the dialog.
  • On completion the dialog "You're all set" will contain "[Environment: Sandbox]".

Note that this will permanently log your purchase. If you do a future test within the sandbox environment, even if you reset the paid status within your app, Restore Purchases will work since you previously made a payment.

Sandbox environment + sandbox account via Xcode

In order to do repeated tests, you need an Apple Sandbox Account. See 'Setting things up' above for creating that. With a sandbox account you can reset purchases and make other changes, though it's not as flexible as local testing using a .storekit file.

  • On your iOS device, you must have enabled Developer Mode.
  • Stay signed in with your regular Apple account.
  • In Settings > Developer, scroll to the bottom and you'll see the heading Sandbox Apple Account. Sign in with a sandbox account.
  • Run your app from Xcode. This will work the same as sandbox environment testing but now you'll see your sandbox account details in the Apple payment dialog footer.

Testing via TestFlight

Sandbox environment testing via TestFlight

All testing done via TestFlight is in the sandbox environment. It will obtain product details from your App Store Account. Now the Apple payment dialog has the title "TestFlight" and the same "For testing purposes only..." message. On completion the dialog "You're all set" will contain "[Environment: Sandbox]".

As with sandbox environment testing via Xcode, all payments made from your Apple account will be permanently logged.

In the original question: "I just want to test the IAP on TestFlight with my testers." You can make your app available to beta testers via TestFlight and they can safely test purchasing within the sandbox environment without being charged. Note what I've said about this being permanently logged though.

Sandbox environment + sandbox account via TestFlight

In order to do repeated tests, you need an Apple Sandbox Account, but there's an extra step compared to testing in Xcode.

See 'Setting things up' above for creating a sandbox account.

  • On your iOS device, follow the same steps as for Xcode: enable developer mode, stay signed in with your regular Apple account, sign in to your sandbox Apple account from within Developer settings.
  • Go to Settings > your Apple account. Tap Media & Purchases and Sign out.
  • Within Media & Purchases sign in to your sandbox account.
  • Now when you test your app installed via TestFlight, the Apple payment dialog has the title "TestFlight", the same "For testing purposes only..." message and the sandbox account in the footer.

Resetting and configuring an Apple sandbox account

The benefit of using a sandbox account is that you can see confirmation of a purchase, clear the purchase history and change settings like Country or Region, Subscription Renewal Rate and whether purchase flow should be interrupted with a requirement to accept updated terms and conditions. You can do all this at App Store Connect > Users and Access > Sandbox.

In my experience, the effect of changing settings is instant and can be retested in your app without restarting it. Clearing purchase history takes a while (maybe 15-30 mins).

Finally...

Note that for sandbox environment testing (via Xcode or TestFlight), there is currently a bug with the currency — the prices obtained by your app show in $ even if you have correctly set your region elsewhere (e.g. United Kingdom, where it should be £). However the currency and price will be correct in the Apple payment dialog.

Q: Select rows with defined value + anything else A:

I can think of two options which should work on most DBMS

Option 1, using GROUP BY with HAVING:

select name
from employee 
group by name
having sum(lang = 'SQL') = 1 
and count(distinct lang ) > 1 ;

  • having sum(lang = 'SQL') = 1 ensures the name appears exactly once with lang = 'SQL'

  • count(distinct lang ) > 1 ensures the same name has at least one additional, different language

Edit

As jarlh mentioned in the comment sum(lang = 'SQL') = 1 will raise an error on most DBMSs. for those DBMSs which do not support the mentioned syntax you could use having sum(case when lang = 'SQL' then 1 else 0 end) = 1

Option 2, using EXISTS:

select name 
from employee e
where lang='SQL'
and exists (select 1 from employee ee where ee.name=e.name and lang <> 'SQL' );

  • Selects names that have lang = 'SQL'

  • EXISTS verifies that the same name also has at least one lang different from SQL
